questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) MODIFIED LANGUAGE READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.
The fundamental economic question is how to meet unlimited wants with limited resources. What is an example of limited resources?

options.A: insufficient consumer goods in the local shops
options.B: insufficient jobs to allow full employment
options.C: insufficient machinery to produce electrical goods
options.D: insufficient tax revenue to finance building a school

questions.questionText: Which statement is not a positive economic statement?

options.A: An increase in the rate of income tax decreases the wish to save.
options.B: An increase in the rate of income tax has a greater impact the greater the level of income.
options.C: An increase in the rate of income tax causes more hours of work to be supplied.
options.D: An increase in the rate of income tax is the fairest way to finance the national health service.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a production possibility curve (PPC). It indicates the combinations of consumer goods and capital goods produced by an economy using all its available resources. units of consumer 40 X goods PPC
The tariff on Indian goods entering the US falls from 10% to 5%. What will be the most likely effect on the producer and consumer surplus in the US? US producer US consumer surplus surplus

options.A: decrease increase
options.B: decrease no change
options.C: increase increase
options.D: increase no change

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the demand for, and supply of, carrots. S price P D O quantity What is true at price P ?

options.A: There will be a shortage of carrots.
options.B: There will be a surplus of carrots.
options.C: There will be an increase in the sale of carrots.
options.D: There will be market clearing of carrots.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the market for hand-made furniture. price of supply hand-made furniture X P Y Z demand O Q quantity Which area of the diagram represents the producer surplus?

options.A: area X
options.B: area X + Y
options.C: area Y
options.D: area Y + Z

questions.questionText: How is the market supply of a product in a competitive market obtained?

options.A: by aggregating the supply of all firms producing the product
options.B: by averaging the supply of all firms producing the product
options.C: by calculating the supply of the typical firm producing the product
options.D: by estimating the supply of the largest firm producing the product

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the demand curve for luxury cars. price D D O quantity The shift in the demand curve D to D can be explained by
What is cross elasticity of demand?

options.A: the responsiveness of price of good X due to a change in demand of good Y
options.B: the responsiveness of quantity demanded of a good due to a change in its price
options.C: the responsiveness of quantity demanded of good X due to a change in quantity of good Y
options.D: the responsiveness of quantity demanded of good X due to a change in the price of good Y

questions.questionText: Consumers receive an increase in their incomes. Which circumstances will cause the quantity of the product sold to increase the most? price elasticity of nature of the product supply of the product

options.A: inferior good price elastic
options.B: inferior good price inelastic
options.C: normal good price elastic
options.D: normal good price inelastic

questions.questionText: An unstable disequilibrium is when a market does not return to an original equilibrium point from a disequilibrium position. The diagram shows a market with two equilibrium points. PO/QO is the original market equilibrium. At which price is the market in an unstable disequilibrium? S A price B C PO D D O QO quantity

The table shows the quantity of a product supplied at two different prices by four firms, A, B, C and D. Which firm has a price elasticity of supply equal to 1 when the price falls from $10 to $8? price of product ($)

To improve its financial position a government decided to reduce expenditure on investment in the public sector. Despite this, there was not a fall in economic growth. What was the most likely effect of the government’s action?

options.A: An original budget deficit was reduced.
options.B: An original budget surplus was reduced.
options.C: Consumer expenditure decreased.
options.D: Public sector productivity decreased.

questions.questionText: An economy has a 20% housing shortage. The government builds 10% more houses for poorer families and fixes the rent below the equilibrium for the market. Which effect will this direct provision have on the market?

options.A: A greater imbalance in the market in private housing will develop.
options.B: Housing waiting lists for poorer families will be cleared.
options.C: The supply of government housing will fall short of demand.
options.D: The supply of private housing for rent will fall by 10%.

questions.questionText: Which statement about nationalised and privatised industries is correct?

options.A: A privatised industry is usually less competitive than a nationalised industry.
options.B: A profitable private company cannot be nationalised.
options.C: Privatisation is a form of monetary policy.
options.D: Privatisation is a way of raising money for the government.

questions.questionText: What is not true about subsidies?

options.A: They are paid to firms.
options.B: They have to be paid back.
options.C: They reduce the cost of production.
options.D: They shift the supply curve to the right.

questions.questionText: What is unlikely to occur with an increase in the provision of public goods?

options.A: consumer non-excludability
options.B: improved use of resources
options.C: opportunity cost
options.D: reduction in tax

questions.questionText: The diagram shows aggregate demand and aggregate supply curves for an economy. general AS price level AD AD O national output What would cause a change in the aggregate demand from AD to AD ?

options.A: a decrease in the budget surplus
options.B: consumption of domestic instead of foreign goods
options.C: government campaigns to encourage household savings
options.D: investment in knowledge-based enterprises

questions.questionText: What would cause a shift in the short-run aggregate supply curve but not the long-run aggregate supply curve?

options.A: advances in technology
options.B: a change in the money wage rate
options.C: emigration of people of working age
options.D: gross investment exceeding depreciation

questions.questionText: Which effect of inflation is described as redistributive?

options.A: the improvement in the terms of trade
options.B: the increased reluctance of people to hold money
options.C: the inconvenience of frequently changing prices
options.D: the loss of purchasing power of people on fixed incomes

questions.questionText: In which situation will a country’s terms of trade worsen?

options.A: The prices of its imports rise by more than the prices of its exports.
options.B: The total value of external payments rises by more than the total value of external receipts.
options.C: The value of its imports rises by more than the value of its exports.
options.D: The volume of its imports rises by more than the volume of its exports.

questions.questionText: Industrialised countries X and Y trade with each other. Country X imposes a general tariff of 20% on imports from country Y. In which circumstances would the imposition of the tariff be unfavourable to country X?

options.A: if country X is seeking to protect its infant industries
options.B: if country X lacks the capacity to produce import substitutes
options.C: if imports from country Y have been dumped in country X
options.D: if imports of manufactured goods from country Y are price elastic

questions.questionText: The diagram shows aggregate supply and aggregate demand curves for an economy. general SRAS price level SRAS X Y AD AD O real output What would cause a movement from X to Y?

options.A: a decrease in income tax and in the cost of production
options.B: a decrease in interest rates and increase in the cost of production
options.C: an increase in income tax and in the cost of production
options.D: an increase in interest rates and decrease in the cost of production

questions.questionText: The table shows changes in the population, price level and Gross Domestic Product (GDP) of a country. year 1 year 2 population (millions) 50 55 Consumer Price Index 100 120 nominal GDP ($ billions) 400 480 What happened to real GDP and real GDP per head between year 1 and year 2? real GDP real GDP per head

options.A: no change fell
options.B: no change rose
options.C: rose fell
options.D: rose rose

questions.questionText: The table shows selected balances from a country’s balance of payments account in 2016. $US billions trade in goods –30 trade in services +10 primary income balance +10 secondary income balance –8 capital & financial flow +15 What was the country’s current account balance in 2016?

options.A: –$3 billion B –$10 billion C –$18 billion D –$20 billion

questions.questionText: What does the Marshall-Lerner condition state must be present for a depreciation of a currency to cause an improvement in the current account balance?

options.A: The price elasticity of demand for exports and the price elasticity of demand for imports are both greater than one.
options.B: The price elasticity of demand for exports and the price elasticity of demand for imports are both less than one.
options.C: The sum of the price elasticity of demand for exports and the price elasticity of demand for imports is greater than one.
options.D: The sum of the price elasticity of demand for exports and the price elasticity of demand for imports is less than one.

questions.questionText: What is most likely to be increased by a policy of increased direct taxes and lower government spending?

options.A: the balance of payments deficit
options.B: the budget deficit
options.C: the rate of inflation
options.D: the level of unemployment

questions.questionText: To encourage people to work, a government increases the minimum income level at which people start to pay income tax. Which types of macroeconomic policy are being followed here? fiscal monetary supply side policy policy policy

A country with low unemployment and a managed floating exchange rate has a persistent current account deficit on its balance of payments. Which policy to reduce this deficit is most likely to keep unemployment low, but cause inflation?

options.A: depreciating its currency
options.B: higher direct taxation
options.C: higher import tariffs
